chapter: Dance tastes, big bands and the boat
title: Dances, carnival balls and playing for Greeks and the Arnold Johnson tour
summary: DeDroit says being commercial meant playing polkas, Yiddish music and five-four Greek music, and recalls touring Ohio and Pennsylvania as feature trumpet with Arnold Johnson's orchestra.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What dances do you remember the people doing specific, like foxtrots, tangos?

Oh, they used to, it's according to who's giving the dance. If it's a company dance or a convention dance, you know. I even played polkas. Because during the carnival season we used to put on a couple of carnival balls away from the auditorium by tourist bureaus, and they'd bring people who liked to dance the music, perhaps that we were not used to playing. But being commercial, and I was commercial, I had everything in the box. I even had Yiddish music, I even had music in five-four time for Greeks, if they wanted to. Most musicians can't play five-four time, but I mean, I could, it's pretty hard. But I was lucky enough to have good instruction. And then when I played for Tom Chamale, he was a Greek, and we'd get to start spot, you know, you know there's a Greek wedding, something like that, we played five-four music. But I didn't play for Tom Chamale as a leader. I was important. He brought me up, he came down here to hear me. I played with a band called Arnold Johnson's Orchestra. And they were under the direction of Paul Weichmann. We toured Ohio, and we toured Pennsylvania. I got tremendous money too. I was the feature trumpet player. And we had a whole season at St. John's Casino and Carl Gables. But, uh, I did.
